keywords.def: the exit point where a letter's sound is made (plural makharij, مخارج)
the nose, where ghunnah comes from

questions.q: Read «مَبْثُوثَةٌ» (88:16) and name the makhraj of each letter.
questions.a: م both lips; ب both lips; ث tongue tip near the top teeth; و rounded lips; ة (taa) tongue tip.

questions.q: Makharij sort (pupil PDF): put 12 letters into throat, tongue, lips or nose. Today's rota group recites 88:6 to 11 to the teacher in turn.
questions.a: Throat: ء ع غ; tongue: ق ل ص ث; lips: ب ف و م; nose: the ghunnah of نّ.

questions.q: Extend: write the four lip letters.
Stretch: which letter in «نَمَارِقُ» (88:15) is from the back of the tongue?
Which letter is made by both lips closing?
questions.a: A) م. م and ب close both lips. ف uses the top teeth on the lower lip; ن is the tongue tip.
top teeth on the lower lip
options: top teeth on the lower lip

questions.q: Think again: Try to say 'baa' with your lips apart. Can you? What does that tell you about where ب is made?
questions.a: You cannot: ب is made by closing both lips. Each letter has its own exit point (makhraj).
